seoTitle: Connect Namecheap Domain to Blogger & Fix 404 Error
metaDescription: Connecting a Namecheap domain to Blogger? Learn the correct DNS records to set and how to fix the common 404 error after connecting your custom domain.
intro: Connecting a Namecheap domain to a Blogger blog gives your site a professional, branded web address, but it commonly runs into a 404 error if the DNS records aren't set up exactly right. This guide walks through the DNS setup in Namecheap and the Blogger configuration needed to avoid that error.

steps.heading: Get the DNS records from Blogger
steps.body: In Blogger's custom domain settings, find the CNAME records Google requires for domain verification and connection.

steps.heading: Add the required records in Namecheap
steps.body: Log in to Namecheap, open Advanced DNS for your domain, and add the CNAME records exactly as provided by Blogger.

steps.heading: Set up the domain in Blogger settings
steps.body: Enter your custom domain in Blogger's settings so it recognizes the domain once the DNS records are verified.

steps.heading: Troubleshoot the 404 error
steps.body: If a 404 error appears after connecting, double-check that the CNAME records match exactly and that there are no conflicting records left over in Namecheap.

steps.heading: Confirm the blog loads on the custom domain
steps.body: Once records propagate, visit your custom domain to confirm your Blogger blog loads correctly without the 404 error.

faq.question: Why do I get a 404 error after connecting my domain to Blogger?
faq.answer: This is usually caused by incorrect or incomplete CNAME records in Namecheap that don't exactly match what Blogger requires.

faq.question: Do I need to change nameservers to connect to Blogger?
faq.answer: No, you typically just add specific CNAME records in Namecheap's DNS settings rather than changing nameservers entirely.

faq.question: How long until my custom domain works on Blogger?
faq.answer: It depends on DNS propagation, which can take anywhere from a few minutes up to 24-48 hours in some cases.

faq.question: Can I use a subdomain instead of the root domain for Blogger?
faq.answer: Yes, Blogger supports connecting a subdomain, which can be simpler to set up than the root domain in some DNS configurations.
